#1994. Chelsea transfer news: The three positions where the Blues need January reinforcements

By Axel Clody | 19 Nov 2026 11:54, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 11:54

Chelsea’s start to the season under Xabi Alonso has been marked by a contradiction that is hard to ignore: while the attack is posting impressive numbers and places the team among the most productive in the Premier League, the defensive system is far from offering the same security.

Chelsea score goals regularly, but also struggle to stop opponents from hitting the net. The result is an unbalanced team that is still looking for an identity capable of sustaining its ambitions in the competition.

After ten games, Chelsea sit fifth with 16 points, from five wins, one draw and four defeats. They have scored 19 goals, the third-best attack in the league, but conceded 16, the seventh-worst defence. The difference between the two areas helps explain why the team still cannot turn its attacking potential into a more consistent campaign.

There is no clear indication yet on whether the club will return to the market in January. The board were very active in the last window, investing more than £340m (€400m) on signings while raising an even larger sum from player sales. The financial balance of the movements was positive, but that does not mean the squad is complete.

Chelsea still have important gaps, some of them highlighted precisely by the difficulties of the first few months of the season. If they decide to make use of the winter window, the London club do not necessarily need another overhaul. Three positions, however, deserve special attention and could receive targeted reinforcements capable of raising the team’s competitive level.

The defence has been Chelsea’s main problem. More than the number of goals conceded, it is the way they happen that is worrying: individual errors, positioning difficulties and a disorganisation that repeats from game to game. The unit lacks a player capable of giving his team-mates security and offering consistency in a team that often allows opponents dangerous situations.

Wesley Fofana has accumulated errors, while Levi Colwill is going through a very negative start to the season. Maxence Lacroix, signed in the last window, has also yet to convince and justify the expectation placed on his arrival. The picture makes it clear that Alonso needs more reliable alternatives to organise the defensive line.

In that context, signing an experienced centre-back, capable of playing in different positions in defence, would be especially interesting. It is not just a matter of adding another name to the squad, but of finding someone who can take responsibility, guide his team-mates and offer tactical solutions to the manager.

Jules Kounde is an example of a profile that could meet that need. The Frenchman has been linked with Chelsea in recent days and faces an uncertain future at Barcelona. Alongside his experience at the highest level, his versatility to play both in the centre and on the right of defence would be an advantage. In a squad that needs more stability, a player of this profile would be an important addition.

Midfield also deserves attention, especially given the way Chelsea ended the last transfer window. The departure of Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City, in a deal that brought in more than £119m (€140m), left a considerable gap on the very last day of the window.

The London club ended a financially busy window without finding a worthy replacement, or at least someone capable of filling part of the Argentine’s importance.

The attempt to sign Lamine Camara was never completed. Chelsea came very close to agreeing a deal in the final hours of the window, but negotiations with Monaco collapsed. As a result, Moises Caicedo remained the main reference in the area, carrying even greater responsibility in building and sustaining the midfield.

The problem is that the Ecuadorian has had physical issues at the start of the season and is not always available. When he plays, he shows the quality to protect the defence and balance the team. The question is finding someone who can share those duties with him.

Valentin Barco appears as an interesting alternative because of his talent, but there is still a gap between recognising his potential and handing him such a big responsibility in the Premier League. The Argentine has not been used much, which also makes it difficult to judge whether he is ready for a bigger role.

Romeo Lavia, for his part, has been a pleasant surprise. The Belgian has the quality to perform the role and has managed a run of games, which is important given the physical problems that marked his last seasons. Even so, his injury history prevents Chelsea from treating his availability as a certainty.

Jordan Henderson offers experience and has appeared as another alternative, but at 36 it would not be reasonable to expect the Englishman to permanently solve the area’s shortcomings.

A good-level midfielder, with the physical capacity and quality to play alongside Caicedo, would give the manager more options and prevent the team’s performance from depending so much on the Ecuadorian’s presence.

The third need is at the head of the attack. Joao Pedro is an essential piece for Alonso, but Chelsea need a more reliable alternative for the moments when the Brazilian is unavailable. The striker’s recent injury again exposed an issue that was already showing in the manager’s choices: the difficulty of finding another player capable of taking on the role with similar confidence.

Danny Welbeck was signed precisely to offer that option. The Englishman did score in the Carabao Cup, but has received few opportunities in the Premier League. Even with Joao Pedro recently sidelined by injury, Alonso turned little to the experienced centre-forward, which raises doubts about how much he is really in plans for more frequent involvement.

It is possible to question whether age weighs in this assessment or whether Welbeck’s style does not exactly match what the Spanish manager is looking for in the position. Whatever the explanation, the fact is that the veteran has yet to establish himself as a reliable alternative to the Brazilian.

Emanuel Emegha also does not appear, at least at the moment, to be the solution Chelsea are looking for. The squad lacks a penalty-box centre-forward who can offer physical presence, attack the last line and turn the chances created by the team into goals. Someone who does not necessarily have to compete with Joao Pedro for a starting place, but who is able to replace him without a significant drop in performance.

#1989. Legendary commentator CLIVE TYLDESLEY on how his ITV exit has made hearts grow fonder, the rise of YouTube streamers, his lockdown money-spinner - and why he refuses to be another loud voice in the game

Published: 02:01 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 14:00 EST, 15 November 2026

Clive Tyldesley reaches for his glasses as he rummages through the commentary charts crammed into an old filing cabinet, jokes about his fading eyesight and supposes one day he will no longer be able to identify footballers from the gantry.

Fortunately, we are still far from that point. At 72, Tyldesley is calling the game as accurately as ever. His eyes are perfectly good when bespectacled, his mind nimble enough to keep up with play and his soothingly familiar voice strong and authoritative with a gentle tendency towards self-deprecation.

This much was evident as Manchester United roared back to beat Roma in the Champions League and a clip of his spine-tingling commentary from the live CBS broadcast circulated on social media and found an appreciative audience in Europe.

'I don't know if there's an element of nostalgia in hearing my voice again,' says Tyldesley. 'If I'm honest, I've dodged the worst of the public's ire with everything including commentators because I haven't been around for the last few years.

'Absence has made a few hearts grow a little fonder towards me and maybe if I'd been on Sky every week for the last six years, I'd be no less unpopular than anybody else out there. So, I can't pretend it's not nice to get some engagement with an audience I used to commentate to on a regular basis, but I'm very happy where I am.'

Tyldesley has been the lead commentator for the CBS coverage of the Champions League since 2020, converting transfer fees into US dollars and keeping his measurements imperial for a North American audience but otherwise approaching the job as he always did.

Clive Tyldesley is calling the game as accurately as ever at 72 and is 'very happy' in his role as the lead commentator of CBS coverage of the Champions League

Tyldesley's commentary of Man United's comeback against Roma circulated on social media and received an appreciative audience in Europe

The 72-year-old wonders whether there was an element of nostalgia to the reaction, with Tyldesley's work for CBS meaning his commentary cannot be shown in Europe

Clips of the studio panel featuring Thierry Henry, Micah Richards, Jamie Carragher and presenter Kate Scott are popular on social media but live action featuring Tyldesley's commentary is governed by broadcasting rights deals and cannot be shown in Europe.

The one from Old Trafford of Matheus Cunha's winning goal in the 86th minute slipped through the net on X and reminded everyone his passion for football is undimmed, and his voice can still stand hairs on attention.

'I don't think I've seen a better game than the first leg of the Paris Saint-Germain v Bayern Munich Champions League semi-final,' says Tyldesley on the rare quality of Europe's elite competition. 'I listened to people with hundreds more England caps than me saying it was bad defending, but I watched the whole game back the next day and it wasn't.

'I'm sorry but it was wonderful attacking and a show of intent by two coaches who trusted defenders to defend one-on-one and attackers to score more than the opposition. Rob Green was my co-commentator and at the end we just put our microphones down and looked at each other and said, "Wow."

'I've not forgotten muddy pitches and assassin centre backs. You only need to look on YouTube to see football was different, but you can't pretend it was better. I see terrible games today just as I did then, but particularly in the Champions League, I regularly stumble upon football that gets me off my seat.'

His exit from ITV, first displaced by Sam Matterface as lead commentator in 2020 and then released entirely after Euro 2024 clearly smarted but Tyldesley is comfortable as the veteran in the fast-changing media landscape.

'Most of the principles I picked up from watching John Motson, Barry Davies and Brian Moore in their pomp are applicable to commentary in 2026,' he says. 'There's no need to reinvent that particular wheel.

'You can offer alternatives such as fan zones and screaming watchalongs for people to view it in a different way. I make it my business to look at J_Tekkz or LDN Movements or whatever is pulling in millions on YouTube.

Tyldesley believes he has not seen a better game than the first leg of PSG's Champions League semi-final with Bayern Munich last year

The veteran commentator believes most of the principles he learned starting out still apply, but admits to having watched popular new voices to see if anything could apply to his commentary

Tyldesley also works as a guest lecturer and commentates for blockbuster computer games, as well as selling framed prints of his commentary charts

'I sample a bit of Mark Goldbridge to see why he's prominent but I'm hearing nothing in those guys applicable to the way I call a football match so I carry on with the same focus I've always had on what constitutes good commentary.'

The central principle being that the game is bigger than the individuals in it, he points out, with viewers tuning in for the football not the commentator.

'The biggest challenge for a television commentator is to find the right words at the big moments, to go beyond "amazing," "brilliant", "incredible" and try to add some editorial context,' says Tyldesley.

'Every goal is unique. The words following a goal that is going to be remembered for years should be unique and specific to that goal, but that's difficult to do. It's unscripted performance and difficult to master and capture.

'I am concentrating hardest for the 10-15 seconds after a big goal because I'm searching for words which will become a small part of people's memories. That's very different to consciously trying to provide 45-second soundbites to amplify one's own personality and standing on social media.

'There's a danger of media leaning that way as it develops such an emphasis on the bitesize.'

Among other things, Tyldesley is a guest lecturer for media students at the University of Salford, still doing commentaries for blockbuster computer games and selling framed prints of his commentary charts, something that started as 'a silly idea in lockdown'.

His wife Susan bought a dozen frames to see how it went. Originally, he offered three Champions League finals won by English clubs in 1999, 2005 and 2012. He sent one each to Gary Neville who played for Manchester United in 1999 and Jamie Carragher who played for Liverpool in 2005. They both posted images online and demand skyrocketed.

'Two good friends,' smiles Tyldesley. 'I probably got about half a million pounds of free advertising out of them.' Sales have soared beyond 50,000. There's a Celtic chart on the gym in Rod Stewart's house. Ant and Dec have bought signed Newcastle charts.

His own venture into podcasting was short-lived and he politely declines between five and ten invitations each week to appear on others.

'I've tried to step back from that kind of thing,' says Tyldesley. 'So much content I hear on football is empty, verbose and repetitive. Really, there are only so many things you can say about Alexander Isak having his shirt pulled in mid-air and Gary Neville probably said most of them in the 30 seconds following the incident.

Tyldesley has no plans to retire and Paramount, the owners of his employers CBS - and soon to be the owners of TNT Sports - will have the UK rights for the Champions League

Sales of his framed commentary charts, something that started during lockdown, have soared beyond 50,000

'There are so many brutally judgmental loud voices in and around football attracting attention that I want to be as far away from as possible, so that's what I do. Unless I sense an opportunity to talk about communication and broadcasting rather than whether club A, B or C should replace their manager. That's not for me Clive.'

So, there's a little less Tyldesley out there than there was. He was content to stay at home and watch the World Cup from his sofa this summer for the first time since 1990.

But there are no plans to retire. And who knows what might change next season when Paramount, the owners of CBS – and soon to be the owners of current rights holders TNT Sports – have the UK rights for the Champions League.

There might be a familiar voice beamed into our living rooms once again.

When I saw the Dear England play, I was the only person in the theatre who didn't enjoy it, and that was because I hated the portrayal of Harry Kane.

He was written as an uneducated numbskull. Written to laugh at and the theatre laughed at him. He was stupid and gullible, another thick footballer.

And anyone who has spent time with footballers will know they might lack for an Eton College education but are streetwise and invariably smart with a razor sharp sense of humour.

Kane is a leader of those men. There's not a single thing about the person Kane has made himself to laugh or sneer at and I wanted to stand up in the theatre that afternoon and shout at everyone.

Oddly, I was introduced to the playwright James Graham at a function a few weeks later and he kind of pushed me for my opinion of Dear England.

I tried to be diplomatic, but I felt so strongly I ended up scolding him for writing a character called Harry Kane who was nothing like Harry Kane.

So, that was the end of a beautiful friendship before it began. And I'm so thrilled now there's a better appreciation of the person Harry is.

#1988. Simon Leslie: Eastbourne Borough five wins from Wembley – and you’re allowed to dream

An early lead in our FA Trophy tie against Chertsey Town, followed by two or three very good chances, had us thinking we might be in for a comfortable afternoon. We were on top, playing well and looking the better side.

Then came the moment that changed everything. A rush of blood saw Nathan Laleye bring down his man. I wasn’t convinced he was the last defender, but referee James Black saw it differently and produced a red card.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Suddenly, a game we had been controlling became a battle to survive, with around 60 minutes still to play with ten men.

Steve King reorganised, sacrificing both Paul McCallum and Darren McQueen, and the boys rolled up their sleeves. Their effort, discipline and determination were outstanding.

They held out admirably until the 85th minute, when Harry Phipps, exhausted after putting in a tremendous shift, left a leg out and conceded a penalty. Chertsey converted, and you could almost feel their energy return.

They huffed and puffed, Lewis Carey made some important saves, and it looked as though we were heading for another penalty shootout.

Then came a moment of magic. A lovely move ended with Tyano Wilson slipping inside and volleying the ball into the net.

The stadium erupted. No penalties required. Just that wonderful feeling football gives you when an afternoon of tension turns into pure joy.

What a performance from a team who had spent most of the afternoon a man short. Those are the days when you learn plenty about your players, and these boys gave us every reason to be proud.

Our reward is a trip to Oxford City in the next round. Only five wins from Wembley. There is plenty of football to be played before we get carried away, but you’re allowed to dream. That’s what the cup is all about.

I just wish more people had been there to see it. You can watch the highlights, but they cannot quite recreate the feeling of being in the ground when that winner went in.

Tuesday’s free-entry game against Littlehampton brought wind, rain and, sadly, a crowd of only just over 400. We dominated the first half but squandered chance after chance and somehow went in at the break at 1-1.

Credit to Littlehampton, who battled valiantly, but our quality shone through in the second half and Borough ran out convincing 6-1 winners, with Tyano Wilson taking the man-of-the-match honours.

Thank you to everyone who braved the weather. We had hoped a free evening of football would tempt a few more through the gates, but we really appreciate those who came. Whether you’re a regular or it was your first visit, we hope to see you again, hopefully in kinder weather.

Tomorrow we travel to Enfield for a clash at the top of the Isthmian Premier table. A proper six-pointer, another big test and another chance for these boys to show what they can do.

Hopefully plenty of you will be there to get behind them. If you can’t make it, Bobby’s commentary will be live so you can follow every kick.

Thank you for your support. Weeks like this remind us why we love this game.

By Matt Law | 19 Nov 2026 11:55, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 11:59

Real Madrid will aim to post a ninth straight win in all competitions when they resume their La Liga campaign at home to Celta Vigo on Saturday night.

Jose Mourinho's side have serious momentum heading towards a period which will see them play eight times before the winter break in Spain halts the season.

There were serious questions asked of Real Madrid following their defeat to Atletico Madrid before the September/October international break, but the response from Mourinho's side to the loss in the Madrid derby has been seriously impressive.

Indeed, Los Blancos have won each of their last eight games in all competitions, including their last five in the league, which has allowed them to sit firmly in the title hunt.

Real Madrid have a record of 10 wins and two draws from their 12 league matches this season, with 30 points leaving them second in the La Liga table, only three points behind the leaders Barcelona, who had been threatening to run away with it earlier this season.

Los Blancos actually have the joint-best defensive record in La Liga this season with only 10 conceded - the same as both Celta and Atletico Madrid.

Real Madrid will have revenge on their minds in this weekend's contest, having suffered a stunning 2-0 defeat to Celta in the corresponding match at Bernabeu last term.

The victory for Celta at Bernabeu last season proved to be their first win over Real Madrid since January 2017, while it was their first league success against Los Blancos since May 2014, with this fixture dominated by the capital giants throughout history.

Celta have been solid defensively this season but have found it incredibly difficult down the other end of the field, netting only 10 times in 12 league matches, which is among the worst attacking records in the division at this stage of proceedings.

That said, Claudio Giraldez's side did manage to put five unanswered goals past Salamanca in the first round of the Copa del Rey on November 13.

Celta's last league match ended in a goalless draw with Levante on November 8, and they currently sit 11th in the table, boasting a record of two wins, seven draws and three defeats.

The Sky Blues are also playing in the Europa League this season, currently sitting 27th in the overall table, picking up three points from their first four games of the campaign.

Real Madrid have been boosted by the news that Aurelien Tchouameni and Bernardo Silva are both back in training ahead of this match.

Tchouameni pulled out of the latest France squad with a groin issue, while Bernardo left Portugal duty early due to an injury problem - both are seen as fit for this match at this stage, although it is unlikely that either will be in the starting side.

The returning Vinicius Junior - back from a domestic suspension - is set to feature down the left, with Yan Diomande, Jude Bellingham and Kylian Mbappe potentially also all starting.

However, Rodrygo (knee), Raul Asencio (leg) and Ferland Mendy (hip) are still unavailable for the capital giants.

As for Celta, all of Ilaix Moriba (knee), Manuel Sanchez (hamstring), Alvaro Nunez (groin), Borja Iglesias (calf), Carl Starfelt (hamstring), Miguel Roman (knee) and Jones El-Abdellaoui (knee) are regarded as doubts at this stage of proceedings.

Ferran Jutgla scored twice against Salamanca in the Copa del Rey last time out, but it is expected that Pablo Duran will be given the nod down the middle.

There is also likely to be a position in the side for the experienced Iago Aspas, who has scored five career goals against Real Madrid.

#1984. Barnsley FC v Sheffield Wednesday: Davis Keillor-Dunn the danger now Owls have worked out his numbers game

Davis Keillor-Dunn's sale – or rather the way the Reds responded to it – is symptomatic of why home fans are so grumpy with their club, with protests against the management planned before and during the televised derby game.

In the short-term, the bigger worry is now he is in blue-and-white stripes, the Owls are belatedly starting to work out how to best use him.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The Wearsider is a versatile forward, which is not always as helpful as it sounds.

At Barnsley he scored 16 goals as a "false nine" last season before joining Wrexham on February’s deadline day. Swallowed up in their squad, he failed to score for the Dragons, and even though David McGoldrick stepped up to find the net in his absence, the failure to spend the fee on a replacement summed up why some home fans plan to chant "Enough is enough" four minutes into Friday’s derby.

After bringing the 29-year-old back to South Yorkshire on loan, Henrik Pedersen used Keillor-Dunn from the right, the left and in the hole before asking him to lead the line, the job his successor Dave Challinor has earmarked for now.

Three goals in as many games, six in his last nine, suggests the Owls are starting to find the right formula.

"With Ali (Al-Hamadi) being out, he's probably the closest," says Challinor when asked if his squad lacks a genuine 'No 9'. "Harry (Gray) I think will develop into a nine, but as an 18-year-old playing in League One, the physical part of that is always going to be tough for him.

"Davo's probably a nine-and-a-half. He can play as a nine but also likes to link the play."

For those not au fait with football's trendy numbers game, a No 9 is a traditional centre-forward who leads the line, either as a targetman or playing off the shoulder of the last defender. A 'ten' plays in the hole behind, and a "false nine" or "nine-and-a-half" flits between the two, as Harry Kane does for England.

And although Challinor spoke after Saturday's 3-0 win over Plymouth Argyle about the need for Keillor-Dunn to get into positions to score proper striker's goals, as he did that day, it does not mean shackling him at the top of the pitch.

"I'm okay with him dropping off," he insists. "The important thing is that when the ball is in certain areas, he gets in the right areas. If the ball is in a wide area, he's a box finisher.

"I've shown him all his goals over the last three years and 90 per cent, 95 per cent, are within the width of the posts in the 18-yard box. If the ball is in a wide area, we want him in the box. That's where he'll finish.

"There's nothing to say that outside of that we don't want him working and running channels.

"As long as the majority of his stuff is in central areas and we're getting the ball to him, if he wants to impact the game in different areas, then great, but only on the odd occasion.

"I'll go back to the Oldham game (Challinor's first as manager, in the FA Cup first round) in the first half. He spent far too much time almost as a left wing-back, which is not playing to his strengths.

"(The message was) go and get close to the goal, he gets a goal, he gets the same on Saturday, another couple of opportunities within that.

"We will give them freedom, but freedom within the structure."

Quite what that structure will be is a challenge for Daniel Stendel's Barnsley players. It is hard for the coach to tell them exactly how the Owls will play when, three games in, Challinor is still working it out.

"We prepare the team for the next opponent every time," says Stendel. "But I think two different things (about Wednesday).

"A new manager has come in, but the quality is the same as before. Maybe some things on the tactical side have changed. We can see some things in the video analysis.

"The other thing is the situation. It's the derby, it's a night game, it's live on TV. It's a lot more than Sheffield against Barnsley and I think that makes the game so different."

Stendel sees it as a no-lose situation for a club with no wins in their last nine League one games and one from bottom.

"The feeling against Leicester and Oxford (two draws), especially when you concede a red card (as they did early in both games), what you can expect against a top team in the league goes down from everybody and you say, 'Okay, we can only win.' The game has this feeling a little bit.

"But there's also a responsibility for Barnsley Football Club to know it is a Yorkshire derby. It's maybe the most important derby for this club.

"It can maybe help to bring energy. We can fight against them more and we can only win in this game."

As for special plans for DKD, "not a lot," he replies, "but it's clear he's a really good player in this league.

"A lot of players know his quality in front of the goal, especially in the box. We have to look after him.

"Wednesday has a lot of quality players but he's surely a player that we have to mark."

#1980. Man City survive tunnel clash and Porto fury thanks to Haaland double

Erling Haaland revealed on the eve of this clash how he loves chopping firewood in his spare time – and his goals set alight Manchester City’s Champions League campaign on a fractious evening in Porto.

So much for the new group stage of the competition taking time to warm up. This clash was a hot-blooded, bitter contest that spilt over in the tunnel at half-time, with players getting separated and tempers rising.

And City were not easing themselves back into European action either, they went full throttle at the start of a tough set of group games. With Enzo Maresca, it looks like it will be all-out attack to get the best out of this team.

They can look nervous at the back, particularly with the ball at Gianluigi Donnarumma’s feet, but have attacking weapons to hurt any team in this elite competition. This was a performance that their rivals will take note of.

“It was a complete performance on and off the ball for 95 minutes,” was Maresca’s assessment.

City will certainly scare the traditional heavyweights with Haaland leading their attack and taking an axe to Porto’s defence like he does with logs in his back garden. It was his 58th and 59th goal in 59 games in the Champions League, with his latest an expertly directed header off a post and a calm side-footed finish.

NO MISTAKE from Erling Haaland this time 💪He's put Man City 1-0 up in Porto 🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/UpKOqQA49s

There is an argument that Pep Guardiola could have achieved more in the Champions League, given City’s dominance in domestic football. They have been knocked out by Real Madrid in the last three seasons but this is a new City, different personnel and even a new look.

They wore their black and yellow away kit, inspired by “Manchester’s iconic worker bee” according to Puma, and grafted their way to victory here. Non-stop running going forward, and scrapping with Porto, too.

The Portuguese champions were not happy with Marc Guéhi’s challenge on Gabri Veiga and claimed an elbow was used, with the row carrying on in the tunnel at half-time with security guards separating the players. Rúben Dias also appeared to nudge a Porto official on his way to the dressing room.

“I didn’t see anything but anyway, you can ask how many times you see me or my bench stand up? Zero, for 95 minutes. How many times do you see their bench? So...” Maresca added.

Only Dias and Haaland remain from the starting line-up from the Champions League triumph three years ago, so this is essentially a new team with a new manager.

Erling Haaland seals the deal in Porto 🤝🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/10xSTtZ8nw

Phil Foden, on as a sub in that game, started at Estádio do Dragão after his horse Wreck It Ronnie defeated Najidi Storm, which started the Goodwood race with 1-33 odds and is now the shortest-priced loser in British racing history. The rest of the team are new to City’s challenge.

That includes Ayyoub Bouaddi, 18, who was part of a £320m midfield refresh following the departure of Rodri, who was named among the Ballon d’Or nominees a few hours before kick-off to highlight the experience and class City have lost.

Bouaddi, who cost £81.4m from Lille, made a good start in his full debut. The Moroccan teenager is neat on the ball and gets around the pitch, with the next step being able to dominate games like his predecessor.

“In his last game he lost two balls and stayed calm and was back in our box,” Maresca said. “This shows how good he is because any player after two [poor] passes panics, but he is just 18. Erling, Rúben, Mateo [Kovacic], they can manage these kind of games better, but you don’t expect it from a guy of 18. I didn’t see him panic.”

By Bouaddi’s side in midfield was Enzo Fernández, who sought to drive forward into space when City counter-attacked. He was among the players who, along with Dias, were reminded of their Benfica history by the home fans.

Diogo Costa tends to be linked with a move to the Premier League every summer, but has been a one-club man for his career so far. But he showed why clubs are looking at him with his first-half saves to deny Haaland and Rayan Cherki.

Porto’s legendary goalkeeper, Helton, was in the press box at half-time and would have been impressed with the saves, although he was not in his seat when Haaland scored the first goal, which came 94 seconds after the restart.

City had worked the ball around the penalty area, with Antoine Semenyo drawing out Costa before laying off to Fernández. Haaland’s header from the cross had such precision that the goalkeeper did not dive as it angled in off a post.

Still, Porto had their chances with Alberto Costa heading wide from a corner and William Gomes charging down a Donnarumma kick – with City’s most nervous moments coming when they passed around their back line.

Man City are living dangerously here! 🫣Donnarumma nearly gifts Porto an equaliser 😬 pic.twitter.com/otIfZTHmdn

But Haaland sealed the win as the game ticked into stoppage time, finding the bottom corner from Rayan Aït-Nouri’s cutback.

“It was an amazing game against the champions of Portugal. We knew it would be a difficult fight, man against man, they are a top team,” Haaland said. “They play amazing football. All the pressure, we have to deliver on the big stage and that’s what we did. We controlled the whole first half, created chances.”

For Maresca, the victory was also a challenge against Porto’s aggression, with the Italian coach adding: “I was very pleased. We know in this kind of game when you come here it’s always difficult or tricky. The environment, the way they grew up, it’s normal, but I think we dealt with that very good.”

Top performance, Enzo 👊✨ pic.twitter.com/ds0f207tpS

“I think we could have scored more goals, especially in the first half. We overall deserved the win and happy with the performance. If you think you can come to a place like this and play and not concede any chances, that is not realistic and it is normal. I am quite lucky as I have a squad of good players. The final whistle is blown and Manchester City begin their Champions League campaign with a 2-0 win in Porto. Erling Haaland’s double gives Enzo Maresca a victory in his first Champions League game in charge of Manchester City.

Enzo has two shots from range in quick succession, one from a free-kick. The free-kick goes just wide and the second is saved by D Costa.

It has been an ill-tempered game and tempers have boiled over again. Rosario and Haaland are involved in a tussle on the floor, which then leads to a mass melee. Haaland and Rosario are both booked for their part in starting that. Haaland is pleased that he got booked but I am not sure why. Both played their part in that melee.

Enzo Maresca’s side will head home with all three points. Ait-Nouri’s cross from the left side of the box picks out Haaland, who first-time shot from 10 yards out picks out the far corner. A clinical finish from Haaland and Manchester City will start their Champions League campaign with a win.

Erling Haaland seals the deal in Porto 🤝🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/10xSTtZ8nw

That is really poor refereeing. Porto are denied two clear fouls before Rosario is then punished for a foul on Enzo, which was a foul but so too were the previous two incidents. Francesco Farioli is then booked for his protestations but you can understand their frustration.

Ait-Nouri has the chance to warp up the three points with an effort from the edge of the box but his shot with his weaker right foot goes narrowly wide.

Nothing comes from the corner as Hwang’s delivery to the front post is dreadful.

Haaland has his fourth headed chance of the game but this one goes over the bar from Ndiaye’s cross. Haaland has scored one of those chances but spurned some good ones.

Down the other end, Fofana, only just on, wins Porto a corner and whips up the home fans.

A final change of the night for Porto sees Fofana replace Veiga. One last roll of the dice from Francisco Farioli.

Whilst Manchester City’s lead is only 1-0, Porto will believe an equaliser is there for them. However, the momentum they were building 10/15 minutes ago has seemingly been lost and the visitors have managed to wrestle back a bit more control.

That is a big chance missed by Pepe. Gimenez receives it down the left and pings a cross to the back post. The cross perfectly picks out Pepe, who fluffs his lines and completely mis-kicks.

Manchester City are making their final two substitutions of the night as Kovacic and Ait-Nouri come on for Bouaddi and Foden. Ait-Nouri looks like he is going to play left wing.

Two more changes for Porto as Silva and M Fernandes are replaced by Gimenez and Moura.

Porto are going to make their first two changes of the night as Hwang and former Norwich man Sainz come on. Varela and Gomes head off.

For the second time in the half, Donnarumma is lucky. To be fair to the Manchester City keeper, the pass back to him is poor but he is then fortunate. His attempted ball out to his left is intercepted by Gomes but it rolls behind for a goal kick. That ball could have rolled straight into the Manchester City net or fallen straight back at Gomes feet with an empty net ahead of him. Donnarumma was very lucky on Saturday against Coventry to avoid a calamitous moment and he is lucky to avoid another awful moment for the second time in quick succession.

Man City are living dangerously here! 🫣Donnarumma nearly gifts Porto an equaliser 😬 pic.twitter.com/otIfZTHmdn

Ndiaye receives it out on the left before driving inside. He gets his shot away from the edge of the box and tries to pick out the far corner but it is too close to D Costa and an easy save for the Porto keeper.

A fine pass from Rosario inside his own half cuts through Manchester City’s midfield sends Varela racing through the Manchester City half. He plays it out to his right to find Gomes, who cuts inside onto his left before trying to beat Donnarumma at his near post but the shot goes wide.

Enzo Maresca responds to a shift in momentum in this game making a double change. Anderson and Ndiaye come on for Cherki and Semenyo.

Porto have started to gain some momentum and they want a penalty. Bouaddi is perhaps a touch fortunate not to be penalised for a foul right on the edge of the box but it may have been just outside the penalty area. You can feel the game starting to turn in Porto’s favour.

Varela is inches away from an equaliser for Porto and plenty of the home fans thought the ball was in the net. Varela sends a curling effort towards goal from the edge of the box but it goes narrowly wide.

That was a glorious chance for Porto to equalise. A corner is sent in from the left to the back post, where Alberto heads it back across goal. However, none of his teammates, including Silva, could tap the ball into the net. Porto should probably be back on level terms.

Donnrumma is a very, very lucky man. Porto would have had a certain penalty as Donnarumma completely flattened Pepe but the latter was offside so it is no penalty. Donnarumma has been booked but avoids a penalty, which would have been a guarantee had Pepe been onside.

Just three minutes into the second half, Enzo Maresca has made a substitution. Gvardiol, on a yellow, is withdrawn and Khusanov is brought on.

Porto’s legendary goalkeeper, Helton, was embracing Daniel Sturridge in the press box and they weren’t in their seats when the goal went in. Lovely move from City and Haaland steered in his 58th goal in the competition.

Haaland wasted two headed opportunities in the first half but he does not spurn this chance. It is a first Manchester City assist for Enzo, who clips in a cross from the left side of the box. Haaland meets it and his header glances off the far post and goes in.

NO MISTAKE from Erling Haaland this time 💪He's put Man City 1-0 up in Porto 🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/UpKOqQA49s

Gabriel Clarke on Amazon Prime has reported that there was some trouble in the tunnel as the two sides went off for half-time. Both sets of security teams for the clubs were forced to step in.

We are back under way in Porto. Tempers were really starting to boil over as that first half wore on so will that continue into the second half?

The former Liverpool, Manchester City and Chelsea striker has described the incident involving Marc Guehi and Gabri Veiga as a “nasty collision” and “it does not look good at all”. I think Guehi is a lucky man to still be on the pitch as some VAR officials would surely have recommended a review for that foul. Porto boss Francesco Farioli felt Guehi led with his elbow and the home fans were not happy with that as well as a number of other decisions in that first half.

Gvardiol needs to be careful as he is not punished for delaying a restart when you consider he is already on a booking. The Porto fans want to see a second yellow but the referee says the ball was moving so Porto could not take the restart.

Three added minutes to conclude this first half.

Should Guehi be in trouble here? He appears in real time to win his header but when you watch the replays he led with his arm. He catches Veiga right in the face and Guehi could be in some strife. Porto fans quick to remind Ruben Dias and Enzo Fernandez of their Benfica history. They jeered the pair when they got on the ball. He can expect more of that in the Premier League after his part in England’s exit at the World Cup, which led to Argentina players holding up a flag saying the Falkland Islands were Argentina’s.

Tensions are boiling over. They have been threatening to do so between Gomes and Gvardiol for a little while and now they do. Gomes steals the ball off Gvardiol and attempts to counter but is pulled back by Gvardiol, who is rightly booked. Gomes is not happy with Gvardiol and they come to blows.

D Costa twice denies Manchester City in a matter of seconds. First he saves from Haaland, then gets to his feet to deny Cherki. Manchester City are knocking on the door and you do feel like a goal is coming for Enzo Maresca’s side.

No goals in Porto but Real Madrid have their second at home against Inter Milan through Fede Valverde.

Manchester City struggled to carve out any genuine chances in the opening quarter of an hour but there are creating more and more opportunities, the latest falling to Foden, whose shot from the right side of the box looking for the far corner is saved by D Costa.

It is not often you see Haaland miss two good chances with his head in quick succession but that is what has happened. He knows he should have done better as he shakes his head in frustration.

Porto’s front three have struggled to have much of an impact in the game, in particular Silva up top, who has been almost non-existent.

A great save from D Costa to deny Haaland. Foden’s cross just before the byline on the left side of the box picks out Haaland. The Norwegian has barely touched the ball tonight but comes close to opening the scoring. However, D Costa is on hand to deny him with a fine save. Should Haaland have given D Costa the chance to save it? Maybe not.

Diogo Costa CLAWS away Erling Haaland's header 🧤Man City come closest so far in Porto 👀 pic.twitter.com/KVnBHdbNlH

In probably the marquee match-up of the night, Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid are taking on Inter Milan at the Bernabeu. Real have just taken the lead through Kylian Mbappe.

Semenyo cuts inside from the left and gets a shot away from the edge of the box but it is straight at D Costa. That was Manchester City’s first shot of the night.

Veiga has a shot saved at the near post by Donnarumma but the offside flag goes up. Veiga and Pep exchange a neat one-two down Porto’s left before Veiga’s effort is saved but Pepe was offside in the build-up.

Manchester City are dominating possession and perhaps it was a ploy by Enzo Marecsa to take it slowly and hog the ball in order to take the early sting out of Porto. They have not had a shot yet and not really threatened the Porto goal but the hosts have not offered much going forward.

The weather in Porto really is horrible, the type of weather you would expect in Manchester in mid-November than Porto in early September.

Porto have a strong defensive record thus far this season but undoubtedly they will be tested a lot more tonight than they are in Liga Portugal. You would also imagine they will have to be clinical in attack as they are unlikely to create as many chances as they do domestically.

With it hammering down, Porto boss Francesco Farioli has swapped his lovely suit that he was wearing pre-game for a tracksuit top and cap. At half-time, he will probably head back in drenched like all the players if he is active in his dugout.

It has been a positive start for Unai Emery’s Aston Villa out in Belgium as they lead Club Brugge 3-1 at half-time.

Enzo Maresca takes charge of his first Champions League game in charge of Manchester City as they have travelled to Portugal to take on Porto at the Estadio do Dragao. These sides last met during the Champions League group stages during the 2020/21 season. Manchester City won 3-1 at home before the two sides drew 0-0 in this stadium.

Manchester City were busy late on in the transfer window, bringing in both Iliman Ndiaye and Enzo Fernandez as they spent nearly £200m on deadline day alone. They come into tonight’s game off the back of three straight Premier League victories to kick off the Maresca era. Maresca has limited Champions League experience as a manager, which came with Chelsea last season. Manchester City have won their opening game of a Champions League campaign in six of the last seven seasons but this will be the first time since 2015/16 that Manchester City embark on a Champions League campaign without Pep Guardiola at the helm.

“It is a hard place to come [Porto],” said Maresca. “They have started really well. In the last 14/15 games in Europe they lost just one, that shows a difficult place to come, but we will try our best and try to win the game. It is a very, very good team. They have different players, but in terms of the team it is very clear in the way they play. They are aggressive without the ball and on the ball, they have a clear style. But we will try our best and try to win the game. The ambition is the same; try to be ourselves and to win games and then we will see.”

Porto, managed by Francesco Farioli, have won every league game so far this season and already sit four points clear at the summit of Liga Portugal. Farioli takes charge of his first game as a manger in the Champions League and the club make their return to the elite European competition after two seasons away.

“We are going to face one of the big favourites to win the competition,” Farioli said. “It will be a game that will demand that we be at our best, and we know that whenever we step onto the Dragão pitch, something special can happen. I am happy to be in the Champions League for the first time at 37 years old. This will be my first game, but we approach every game with the same attention to detail and the same focus. It is easy for the players to be motivated tomorrow [tonight]. But the key will be our strategy and our ability to execute it, individually and collectively.”

Porto were in the Europa League last season, making it to the quarter-finals, where they were knocked out by Nottingham Forest 2-1 on aggregate. The omens would not appear to be on Porto’s side tonight; they have only won two of their last 16 games against English opposition in major European competition.

#1979. Dave Challinor reveals his deep thinking on Sheffield Wednesday's Barry Bannan

Bannan started Challinor's first league game as Owls manager in the hole, but the latter says it was a horses for courses decision.

"We've not got a load of midfielders but they do bring different things," he argued ahead of Friday's League One game at Barnsley. "I think Barry can play in different roles.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

"For how we want to play at times and have control, him playing centrally and at times a little bit deeper is something for him because of his technical ability.

"I think it will work really well and will probably extend his career depending on how long he wants to play for because there'll be less demand on him influencing the game higher up.

"His strength is his weakness because he wants to influence games and win games at times by himself and put himself in areas where he thinks he can do that.

"Sometimes that can be a detriment of the team.

"I suppose the luxury we have at the minute is we're able to at times ask him to be a little bit more disciplined but on other occasions let him be a little bit of a free spirit.

"When he's higher up he can roll into wide areas, he can come deeper if he wants.

"But we're going to have to find different things at the minute because we don't have the players specifically fit in the positions that we'd like to have.

"We've just got to be careful we don't leave Davo (centre-forward Davis Keillor-Dunn) isolated.

"Something I looked at before I came into the club was a lot of people wanting to come towards the ball.

"The responsibility of the back players and the midfield players is to give the ball in the areas where they can hurt teams."

#1978. Plymouth Argyle vs Peterborough United - prediction, team news, lineups

By Carter White | 19 Nov 2026 11:56, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 20:47

Aiming to avoid back-to-back league defeats, Plymouth Argyle welcome Peterborough United to Home Park for a League One clash on Saturday afternoon.

The Pilgrims were dispatched at the base of title-chasing Sheffield Wednesday last weekend, whereas Posh are in the midst of an on-field crisis despite a recent managerial change.

After missing out on the League One playoffs on the final day of last season, Plymouth Argyle are desperate to crash the top-six conversation this time around; however, a recent result certainly brought supporters back down to Earth.

The Pilgrims were enjoying a four-game unbeaten run (W3 D1) across all competitions before a harrowing afternoon at Hillsborough last weekend, when goals from Billy Mitchell, Davis Keillor-Dunn and Di'Shon Bernard secured a comfortable 3-0 success for Sheffield Wednesday.

Now looking to dodge consecutive defeats, Tom Cleverley's side are currently occupying sixth position in the League One table, just six points behind pacesetters Huddersfield Town and Stockport County in first and second respectively.

The Devonshire outfit are unbeaten across their past three home matches against Reading (0-0), Alvechurch (4-0) and Swindon Town (2-1) in all competitions; however, Plymouth have actually collected more points away from Home Park this season.

The summer departure of fans' favourite Lorent Tolaj to Bristol City has increased the goalscoring burden on Canadian marksman Aribim Pepple, who has netted on five occasions in League One during 2026-27.

In April 2025, Peterborough United experienced one of the proudest days in their humble history, beating a record-breaking Birmingham City side at Wembley Stadium to earn consecutive EFL Trophy crowns.

Eighteen months on, the Posh are enduring a severe fall from grace, with club chairman Darragh MacAnthony admitting that his side are not performing anywhere near the levels expected at the moment.

The form table strongly supports MacAnthony's argument, with Peterborough losing each of their past four competitive matches without finding the net, suffering embarrassing losses to Reading (0-5) and Luton Town (0-3) since the start of November.

Winning just two of his opening nine games in charge, head coach Robbie Savage has failed to turn the tide at Weston Homes Stadium as of yet, with Saturday's visitors sitting in 22nd spot in the League One rankings.

Looking on the positive side, an unexpected victory in Devon could take Posh out of the relegation zone this weekend, with Peterborough victorious on their most recent trip to Plymouth in September 2025.

Peterborough United form (all competitions):

Plymouth will be without the services of defender Alex Mitchell, who remains sidelined due to an unspecified muscular injury.

The absence of the 25-year-old adds to the Pilgrims' backline issues, with Spaniard Julio Pleguezuelo unavailable because of a calf problem.

As a result, Wes Harding, Mathias Ross and Alex Hatridge are the hosts' only centre-back options for Saturday's clash.

Tom O'Connor injury-plagued 2026 continued earlier this week, with Peterborough's Irish defender picking up another hamstring injury in the loss at Luton.

The 27-year-old is set to be sidelined for up to six weeks, joining youngster Lucca Mendonca in the medical room.

Plymouth Argyle possible starting lineup:

Cooper; Harding, Ross, Hartridge; Curtis, Boateng, White, MacKenzie; Amaechi, Ibrahim; Evans

Peterborough United possible starting lineup:

Bass; Dornelly, Hughes, Feeney, Mills; Kelly, Garbett; Shofowoke, Williams, Khela; Leonard

After the disappointment of defeat by Sheffield Wednesday last weekend, Plymouth are now presented with a great opportunity to respond at Home Park.

In the midst of crises on the pitch and in the medical room, Peterborough are hurtling towards a fifth consecutive loss in all competitions.

#1977. No 'knee-jerk reactions': Doncaster Rovers boss Grant McCann on owners and a welcome squad boost

There were no knee-jerk reactions in 2025-26 and Rovers chief McCann counts himself as fortunate to be working at a club where the bigger picture is taken into consideration.

After just under a third of the current League One campaign, Rovers find themselves in the final relegation place – in a position not too dissimilar to last November.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

McCann, whose side visit derby rivals Bradford City on Saturday, said: “Look, I've got a really good relationship with Terry (Bramall) and Gavin (Baldwin).

“I don't need to seek any sort of assurances. That's not the type of person I am really. If they think they need to give me some assurances, they'll always speak to me.

“But what I've got is a really supportive owner and chief executive at a really supportive football club and we're certainly not a knee-jerk reaction type of place.

“That runs right through the club and that's what we've sort of built over the last three and a half years.”

After a well-timed international break following awful away episodes in league and cup at MK Dons and Kidderminster Harriers, Rovers now face back-to-back Yorkshire derbies.

Following the weekend date at Valley Parade, McCann's side host Huddersfield Town next Thursday.

Some welcome news on the injury front has seen experienced duo Matty Pearson and James Collins return to training.

Pearson has made just two appearances this term, with double hernia surgery preceding a calf injury. Loan forward Collins is yet to make his debut.

The 35-year-old has been recuperating from a long-term knee injury sustained last season with parent club Lincoln City, with Rovers conscious that it would take time for him to return to full fitness. James Husband and Tommi O'Reilly are also back in training.

McCann said: “Two Yorkshire derbies in the first five or six days is a brilliant couple of games for us to come back into after the break.”

But with 5,700 away fans expected to make up a third of the crowd and much more concentrated in the away end, Slicker says their Barnsley counterparts have an important part to play, just as they did when the young team battled to win a point against Oxford United despite a ninth-minute red card for Jack Shepherd.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

"I go back to the example of the Oxford game when we conceded and you feel the lift almost from the crowd and it was refreshing," says the goalkeeper. "It did give us that almost second wind.

"Whether it's the home crowd, the away crowd, I think there's a buzz from both. There might be a few beer bottles up at my head or whatever but I thrive off that (atmosphere) and I'm excited for being at both ends of the pitch.

"The crowd is there, you feel it but in reality, it doesn't change my focus.

"You could have no people watching, you could be training, but still as focused as what I will be whenever really.

"You might hear more and even the communication might be different but I think it's still focused, even more focused maybe.

"Communication as a goalkeeper is one of the most important aspects. I'm going to try and communicate whether the boys hear it or not.

"They might be quite glad that they're not hearing my voice."

Stendel is without the suspended Cameron McGeehan and Luca Connell is a doubt with illness, so he hopes the fans can compensate.

"What I would like is that we have a big support in the game," he says. "Not just because it's a derby but also these young guys, without the captain (McGeehan), need the push from the stands.

"It was really positive in the last big game against Oxford here. With ten men after nine minutes, they pushed the team so much."

This is Slicker's first South Yorkshire derby, and he is fully aware of its importance.

"When I first joined, looking at the stadium, I walked around sort of imagining it full,” he recalls.

"There's a lot of (Yorkshire) derbies in League One but Sheffield Wednesday will be the big one – one of, if not the biggest, game of my career.

"I played for Scotland internationally. This will probably be a similar level to it."

If a win would do wonders for Barnsley's belief after nine games without a league victory, wins at Oakwell are special for away teams who bring a big following.

"In terms of an away stand, for a big club, it's a brilliant one," comments Sheffield Wednesday manager Dave Challinor. "That end will be full, it won't be half in one bit, half in the other.

"It's a huge stand. We've got to make the biggest advantage of that we can."

#1971. Barnsley FC supporter groups highlight issues of concern ahead of key meeting with Neerav Parekh - and need for answers

The meeting, chaired by Barnsley FC Supporters Trust, included representatives from Athersley Reds, East Dene Reds, Hoyland Reds, Eaden’s Bar Reds, Manx Reds, Matchday Drinkers and the Fan Advisory Board, along with supporters active on Facebook and season-ticket holders.

Following several weeks of conversations between the trust and the club, it has been decided that Barnsley chairman Neerav Parekh will meet supporter group representatives in early December ahead of speaking to the media.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

A wider fans forum, open to all supporters, will follow before the end of the season.

Issues raised at the meeting included concerns about the long-term strategy and future of the football club and a perceived lack of transparency and communication from the club's leadership and absence of football experience in the day-to-day running of the club.

The club's recruitment strategy was also called into question alongside a decline in match-day experience and attendances.

Questions regarding the club's search for a new chief executive officer - following the departure of Jon Flatman - were also aired alongside the skillset that the club will be looking for in terms of his permanent replacement.

A trust statement read: "It was a productive meeting, constructive in spirit but challenging in discussion. Frustrations were aired openly, yet what came through just as clearly was a shared passion for Barnsley Football Club and a commitment to seeing it prosper rather than decline.

"Much of the discussion centred on the last four years and what the future could look like. Before it began, we set out the financial headlines from that period, so that everyone in the room was working from the same information.

"The club’s four most recent sets of accounts, covering 2021/22 to 2024/25, show a combined operating loss of £28.6 million.

"We believe shareholders have invested in the region of £22 million since 2022, and the chairman, Neerav Parekh, now holds 66.36 per cent of the club’s holding company and 85.2 per cent of its A shares, giving him effective control.

"Some in the room acknowledged that, given those figures, removing the current ownership without a successor able to match that level of investment would pose a greater risk to the club’s future than the present situation."

Addressing the news regarding the meeting with Parekh, the statement continued: "Whilst we look forward to that meeting, it will only be as valuable as the answers it provides.

"Before then, there is a derby to play. Sheffield Wednesday come to Oakwell on Friday night, and we ask every supporter to get behind the players.

"Let’s make sure nobody leaves the ground in any doubt about what Barnsley Football Club means to this town and to its supporters."

Second-from-bottom Barnsley are winless in nine league matches – having taken two points from the last 27 available in League One.

The Reds have not played in the fourth tier of English football since 1978-79.

#1969. Super Mario! Dons hand rebuild job to Swiss success story Frick

Published: 14:14 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 14:45 EST, 15 November 2026

Aberdeen have appointed former Liechtenstein international Mario Frick as their new head coach.

The 52-year-old will take charge at Pittodrie, subject to the completion of UK visa formalities, following a successful spell with Swiss side FC Luzern.

Frick arrives in the north-east after five years in charge of Luzern, where he transformed the club’s fortunes after taking over in December 2021 with the team rooted to the bottom of the Swiss Super League. He guided them away from relegation trouble before leading them to a fourth-place finish and qualification for European football.

Announcing the appointment, Aberdeen chief executive Adrian Bevington said the club had undertaken an extensive recruitment process before selecting Frick as the man to lead the Dons forward.

Bevington said: 'We are delighted to welcome Mario Frick and his assistant coach Roman Matter to Aberdeen Football Club.

'Mario has significant experience as a head coach and has delivered impressive results with both Vaduz and Luzern. He has a proven track record of building competitive teams and developing young players.

'Throughout our discussions, he demonstrated a clear vision, strong leadership qualities and a deep understanding of what is required to build a successful team.'

Sporting director Lutz Pfannenstiel also welcomed the appointment and believes Frick has the qualities to make a major impact at Pittodrie.

Pfannenstiel said: 'Mario is a strong personality with clear ideas about how he wants his teams to play. He brings energy, ambition and a winning mentality, and knows how to build a strong team environment.

Aberdeen have appointed Mario Frick as their new manager

'We were looking for the right person to lead the next chapter of Aberdeen FC, and I’m convinced Mario has the qualities, character and vision to make a real impact.'

Before his spell with Luzern, Frick managed FC Balzers and FC Vaduz, winning promotion to the Swiss Super League with the latter. Across almost 290 senior matches as a head coach, he built a reputation for developing young talent, handing top-flight debuts to more than 30 academy players.

As a player, Frick represented clubs including FC Basel, FC Zürich, St Gallen, Grasshopper, Siena and Ternana. A striker who could also operate in defence, he won 125 caps for Liechtenstein between 1993 and 2016 and remains his country’s record goalscorer with 16 international goals.

Frick said: 'I’m excited to be joining Aberdeen FC. It’s a club with a proud history, passionate supporters and big ambitions.

'Together with the staff, my aim is to create an environment where the players can thrive, develop and perform at their very best, while working towards our goals as a team.'

Frick and assistant coach Matter are expected to arrive in Aberdeen at the start of the week and will begin preparations for next weekend’s Premiership clash with Kilmarnock.

After an impressive fourth-placed finish in the Scottish Premiership last season under Jens Berthel Askou, Motherwell secured European football and earned widespread praise for their attacking style of play.

However, Askou left Fir Park over the summer to take charge of Toulouse, with the North Lanarkshire club appointing Swedish coach Alfred Johansson as his replacement, although he has so far struggled to build on the progress made during the 2025-26 campaign.

After 13 Scottish Premiership matches, the Well sit ninth in the table with three wins, four draws and six defeats, having conceded 21 goals, with only three sides shipping more, while just three teams have scored fewer than their 14.

Despite their worrying start to the new season, Motherwell entered the final international break of the year on the back of a three-match unbeaten run, with draws against St Johnstone and Dundee United either side of a narrow 1-0 victory over St Mirren on Halloween.

While that positive end to October and start to November has offered some encouragement to Johansson's side, they will know they must pick up where they left off before the two-week break to create more breathing room above the bottom two and close the gap on the teams higher up the table.

As for Rangers, they appear to have put their difficult start under Derek McInnes behind them, with the Gers heading into the busy festive period in a strong position to challenge for silverware and close in on rivals Celtic in the Premiership title race.

McInnes's side entered the break with a 2-0 away victory over St Mirren, courtesy of goals either side of half-time from Ryan Naderi and Dan Neil, extending their unbeaten run to 12 matches and marking their first defeat-free spell since August, which has also included two victories over their bitter Glasgow rivals.

This impressive turnaround has followed an early European exit and a difficult start to their domestic campaign under the former Hearts boss, but Rangers are now showing significant signs of improvement compared to recent seasons.

At this stage last year, the Gers were fourth in the table and had recently replaced Russell Martin with Danny Rohl, following another difficult managerial spell, while they had also been sitting third 12 months earlier, highlighting the progress McInnes has made since taking charge.

Despite their recent resurgence, Rangers remain four points behind Celtic, although a victory on Saturday would cut that gap to a single point, with a game in hand on the league leaders still to come.

The sides meet for the second time this season following Rangers' narrow 1-0 victory at Ibrox in early September, with the Gers having since turned their home ground into something of a fortress, as no side has taken a point off them there since their defeat on matchweek two.

Motherwell could name the same starting XI that drew 1-1 with Dundee United, although they remain without several first-team players through injury.

Alex Lowry, Johnny Koutroumbis and Dylan Williams are all expected to miss out due to knee, muscle and hamstring problems respectively, although the trio could return by the start of December.

Lukas Fadinger has scored twice in his last two appearances, albeit both goals coming from the penalty spot, and is expected to anchor the midfield while wearing the captain's armband once again.

Meanwhile, the visitors make the short journey south with a longer list of injury concerns, although they at least avoided any fresh setbacks during their victory over St Mirren.

McInnes will remain without Ross McCrorie, Cameron Devlin, Daisuke Yokota, Lawrence Shankland, Youssef Chermiti and Jose Cifuentes, although Chermiti is the only one of the injured players expected to remain sidelined into 2027.

Paulsen; Sparrow, Girdwood-Reich, Moormann, Longelo; Hodge, Fadinger; Maswanhise, Said, Kanga; Palmer-Houlden

Pandur; Sterling, Makhanya, Fernandez, Penrice; Bouanni, Neil, Raskin, Kim Min-Su; Naderi, Kelsy

Motherwell head into the fixture with some encouraging momentum after going three matches unbeaten, but we expect their progress to be halted by an in-form Rangers side, who should secure their ninth league victory of the season and further close the gap on Celtic.

#1962. Liverpool: Why Brajan Gruda would be perfect Mo Salah successor

By Axel Clody | 19 Nov 2026 12:41

Brajan Gruda has been one of the revelations of the start of the season with Leipzig and Germany. His profile appears ideal to strengthen Liverpool’s attack.

An attacking midfielder by training, Brajan Gruda is shining at the start of the season as a right winger. After a disappointing spell at Brighton, the 22-year-old German bounced back last winter at RB Leipzig. He has been loaned this season by the English club to the German side. Leipzig will sign him permanently in 2027 for £25.5m (€30m). Gruda will then receive a contract until June 2031.

That transfer does not mean he will stay long at Leipzig, however. According to Sky Sport Germany, Bayern Munich have the Germany international on their shortlist. The Bavarian club have not planned any move in this case, unless Michael Olise were to leave. It must be said that, all things considered, the profiles of the two players are quite similar.

Beyond the fact that they are left-footed number 10s shining on the right side of the attack, they are technical players who are rather fond of assists. Brajan Gruda is the fourth player in Europe’s top five leagues with the most successful dribbles at the start of this season, with 36.

He is very efficient in this area, succeeding with 70.6% of his dribbles, a better ratio than Lamine Yamal (58.3%) or Kylian Mbappe (59.7%), who nevertheless attempt more. Beyond dribbles, the 22-year-old is also decisive, with two goals scored and five assists delivered in 13 games for Leipzig.

Those performances opened the doors of the Germany national team. Jurgen Klopp did not hesitate to give him his first two caps, starting him against Serbia (3-1 win) and the Netherlands (5-0) during this November international break. Gruda shone with a solo goal against the Serbs, as well as another goal and two assists against the Dutch.

His feat against Serbia impressed his manager. ‘It’s completely crazy. The defender in front of him? Poor guy!’ - the German manager exclaimed.

On the pitch, in those two games, his understanding with Florian Wirtz, playing as number 10, was also highlighted. Could the two men therefore be reunited at Liverpool?

Liverpool did not sign a genuine right winger this summer, after the departure of Mohamed Salah. Left-footed, technical and provocative, Brajan Gruda has an interesting profile to replace the Egyptian star. He is capable of long solo runs and of shining in tight spaces, relying on his silky left foot. He is a player who has emerged in recent months.

Liverpool therefore seem to have every interest in quickly getting their hands on the Leipzig player. Indeed, if he continues to perform at this level, his market value, which stands at £23.8m (€28m), should rise considerably, while new European heavyweights, in addition to Bayern Munich, will take an interest in his profile.

In this case, Liverpool have two allies who could push Brajan Gruda to join the English giants: Florian Wirtz and Jurgen Klopp.

#1961. Nascar, Nets, Big 12 and MSE: Yormark’s appointment and how he can help Milan

AC Milan were introduced to a new name this week: Brett Yormark. But who is he and what does he bring to the table?

With Milan’s announcement of a new company – Milan Sport and Entertainment – a new CEO was appointed to oversee things and develop the Milanese sporting project for RedBird and that CEO is Yormark.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

For those who are unfamiliar with the new hire, he is obviously someone that Gerry Cardinale trusts heavily and this was stated in the American’s announcement of the MSE company.

“Today, we apply this experience on a different scale: not just to a single club, a single sport, or a single facility, but to an entire city and a portfolio that spans sports, lifestyle, and entertainment. I have known Brett Yormark and worked with him for 25 years.

“We’ve been working with Milan for years, and I can’t imagine a better executive in the international sports industry to help execute this strategy. Thanks to Brett, we can bring the best of American sports and live entertainment to Milan, helping write a new chapter in the city’s growth and international success.

“With AC Milan as our cornerstone, which will always be the driving force behind all our initiatives, we intend to build a world-class sports and entertainment platform capable of shaping the future of Milan and European sports, and bringing it back to the forefront of the global stage.”

However, what has his career looked like so far and how can he help the Rossoneri take the next level?

In terms of his own reputation, he started his career working in selling TV time before moving to be a senior accountant at Palace Sports and Entertainment, sound familiar? From there, he got his first major move, becoming a director of marketing at NASCAR, where he stayed from 1998 to 2005.

After his early experience in basketball, he then moved away from the track and back onto the court where he joined the Brooklyn Jets as their new CEO. Tasked with transforming the club into a more modern brand, he franchised the club – taking them from Brooklyn to New Jersey – and brought several sports and events to the Barclays Center, which opened in 2012, as Sportico reported.

From there, he then headed to Roc Nation, taking a role as their ‘President & Chief of Branding and Strategy’. From artists to athletes, Yormark worked with some of the biggest names and brands in the world from 2019 to 2022 and was a major part of the brand earning the rights for the Super Bowl halftime shows.

It’s worth noting that he’s also worked with Milan in this period, as they partnered in 2020. On a side note, it’ll be interesting to see if these links help any further with the ongoing speculation about the Diavolo and Endrick, who is also represented by the brand.

To join the Milan Sports and Entertainment company, he leaves behind a role with Big 12, where he had held a role since the summer of 2022. Within his first few months as its commissioner, he secured media rights deals with ESPN and Fox to help stabilise the league.

The Kansas City Star continues, stating that he also oversaw expansions into ‘Arizona, Arizona State, Colorado and Utah’, as well as keeping men’s and women’s basketball in Kansas City.

Given that he’ll be working heavily with the hope of making a Milan NBA team, this is relevant experience. Importantly, too, he has already fought for sport in Kansas City, so doing the same for football (and basketball) in Milan will not be unfamiliar territory.

Furthermore, alongside Cardinale, he has experience in getting the most out of TV deals, so this should help the entertainment side of the company take off as well.

Although he’s not got a background in football, the quality of his CV is undeniable and he’s thrived alongside the companies where he’s worked for years.

He’s very confident about the future, stating he’s moving on to a ‘great opportunity’ and that the opportunity of working within the MSE ‘is as big as we want it to be’, as Sportico relayed. It’s a bold statement, but he’s no stranger to delivering.

Leeds United defender James Justin has warned Chelsea have talent “spilling out” as the sides prepare to meet in the Premier League.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Xabi Alonso’s men are due to host Leeds again tomorrow (November 21) and Justin has made it clear a stern test lies ahead.

He told Premier League Studios, as quoted by the official Leeds website: “I feel like it will be a bit of a different side than what we faced in the League Cup tie, and we know they are a team that likes to play in the small spaces.

“They have got talent spilling out and you have to keep control of that but also try and take advantage of somewhere they might not be as tight, obviously.

Leeds returned to winning ways prior to the international break, defeating Chelsea’s London rivals Tottenham Hotspur 1-0.

Justin said: “It has been nice to rest and recharge a little bit, and work on a few things on the training pitch. We are ready to go and pick things up again.

“I would say from last season we have come on leaps and bounds and the confidence that everyone has in the squad is a lot more compared to this time last season. We have still got a way to go but we have had a solid start.”

Leeds showed ambition with their summer transfer window recruitment, splashing out a club-record £40m on England international goalkeeper James Trafford.

They also bolstered in the centre of defence by recruiting Tarik Muharemović and Nico Elvedi, who have been partnering Justin in a back three.

Justin said: “We obviously added some quality players in the summer. We are looking at this season and first and foremost to cement our place in the Premier League. Who knows what can happen after that.

“We had a few rocky results before [Spurs] and maybe didn’t quite get the results that we were looking for or deserved, which happens in football. Sometimes you are going to win games you don’t deserve and vice versa.

“The Premier League is difficult. The game changes in tiny moments and teams are so closely matched that all it takes is one lapse of concentration or one moment of magic to break the deadlock. Then, you are chasing the game and every team can defend well in the Premier League.

“We are more on the front foot in most of the games and looking for ways to decide the game and taking the initiative. That is something that we would like to continue this season and it will be no different traveling to London this weekend.”
